reports.title: Emergency department note
reports.text: 58-year-old male presented to the ED with chest pain radiating to the left arm, associated with shortness of breath and diaphoresis. Denies nausea. An ECG showed ST elevation in the anterior leads. Troponin was elevated at 4.2. He was given aspirin and heparin and taken for emergent cardiac catheterization, which revealed 95% LAD occlusion. A drug-eluting stent was placed. History of hypertension. Plan: admit to CCU for monitoring.

reports.title: Discharge summary
reports.text: Admitted on 03/02 with chest discomfort and diagnosed with anterior STEMI. Underwent PCI with stent placement to the LAD. Hospital course was complicated by atrial fibrillation on day 2, treated with metoprolol. Echocardiogram showed reduced ejection fraction of 40%. No further chest pain. Patient was started on atorvastatin, clopidogrel, and lisinopril for hypertension. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up in cardiology clinic in 2 weeks. Recurrent ischemia should prompt return.

reports.title: Cardiology clinic follow-up
reports.text: Seen in clinic for follow-up after STEMI treated with stent on 03/02. Reports no chest pain but mild fatigue. Continues atorvastatin and clopidogrel. Metoprolol was stopped after atrial fibrillation resolved. Repeat echocardiogram shows improved ejection fraction of 50%. Hypertension is well controlled on lisinopril. Plan to enroll in cardiac rehabilitation.

reports.title: Admission note
reports.text: 72-year-old female with COPD presented with three days of productive cough, fever and worsening dyspnea. She is a former smoker. On exam, crackles at the right base. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe pneumonia. Blood cultures were drawn and she was started on ceftriaxone and azithromycin. Albuterol nebulizers were given for wheezing. Supplemental oxygen was initiated for hypoxia. She will be admitted to the medical floor.

reports.title: Chest X-ray report
reports.text: CHEST X-RAY. INDICATION: pneumonia in a patient with COPD. FINDINGS: Consolidation in the right lower lobe, consistent with pneumonia. Small pleural effusion. Pneumothorax is absent. No pulmonary edema. Hyperinflation and emphysema are noted. A nasal cannula is in place. Compared with the prior study, the opacity has progressed. IMPRESSION: Recommend follow-up radiograph in six weeks to confirm resolution.

reports.title: Primary care visit
reports.text: 54-year-old male with type 2 diabetes presents with polyuria and blurred vision for two weeks. HbA1c was elevated at 9.4%. Creatinine rose to 1.8, concerning for diabetic nephropathy. Denies chest pain. He has been taking metformin but admits to poor adherence. Insulin glargine was started and metformin will be held due to renal impairment. Urine albumin and renal ultrasound are ordered.

reports.title: Renal ultrasound report
reports.text: RENAL ULTRASOUND. INDICATION: renal impairment in a patient with diabetes. FINDINGS: Both kidneys are echogenic with cortical thinning. Hydronephrosis is absent. A simple cyst is seen in the right kidney. Renal artery stenosis cannot be excluded without Doppler. IMPRESSION: Findings consistent with chronic kidney disease, likely from diabetic nephropathy. Recommend nephrology referral and repeat ultrasound with eGFR monitoring.

reports.title: Discharge summary
reports.text: Admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by a urinary tract infection. Initial glucose was elevated at 520 with anion gap acidosis. Treated with insulin infusion and IV fluids; ceftriaxone was given for the UTI. Acute kidney injury on background chronic kidney disease improved with hydration. Blood glucose normalized and he was transitioned to insulin glargine. Metformin remains discontinued. Discharged with nephrology follow-up.
